producer.summary: Producer describes pure juniper scent, tangy crisp citrus, sweet floral aroma, a hint of peppery spice, subtle bitter fruit and a racy finish. Batch-distilled, unfiltered, 47 botanicals (several from the Black Forest such as spruce, lingonberries, sloe and elderflower), rested in earthenware.

critics.palate: Forest fruits with wildflower and island spice notes; juniper present but not dominant.
critics.finish: Balanced, long and rich.
critics.summary: Calls it an exquisite gin that pushes the limits of flavor in the category.

critics.nose: Prominent juniper with intense herbal notes: dried rosemary, cloves, dried mushroom.
critics.palate: Fresh rosemary, evergreen, black pepper and a big forest-floor, earthy, campfire-ember element; fruit (blueberry, orange, apple, peach) emerges late.
critics.finish: Sweet, fruity, slightly tart; very easy drinking.
critics.summary: Graded A- (letter grade). Calls it bizarre, fun and wholly unique. Reviewed at 94 proof.

critics.nose: Very complex: mentholated juniper, pineapple sage, lemon verbena, lavender, rose, shifting as it warms.
critics.palate: Minty and herbal with herbaceous juniper, blackthorn, lavender and pepper; thick, rich mouthfeel.
critics.finish: Oily aromatic herbs, peppermint, lemon balm and blackberry; fresh and fruity.
critics.summary: Main critique is that the contemporary profile sidelines juniper; still recommended as an indulgence.

facts.mash_bill: Molasses-based spirit; 47 botanicals incl. juniper, lingonberry, blackberry, pomelo, chamomile, sage, angelica, coriander, spruce

notes: Input name misspells Schwarzwald. Producer notes are a single descriptive sentence, not split nose/palate/finish. Region from Distiller/producer Black Forest framing.

producer.nose: Prominent Douglas fir and California bay laurel with subtle citrus.
producer.palate: Sage and wok-roasted coriander evoke hillside scrub; angelica root and Saigon cinnamon add earthy undertones.
producer.finish: Clean and crisp with forest-like complexity.
producer.summary: Woodsy, aromatic gin meant to evoke the California landscape. Fir and sage distilled separately; bay laurel and juniper vapor-infused; other botanicals in the pot.

critics.nose: Bold Douglas fir with sage growing more present over time.
critics.palate: Full-bodied; juniper subdued, little citrus.
critics.finish: Peppery.
critics.summary: Spicy, herbal gin suggested for a Gibson or Bramble.

critics.nose: Pine cones, pine needles and sage.
critics.palate: Brawny pine resin with eucalyptus and sage.
critics.finish: Bone dry with pine resin.
critics.summary: Fir-pine character leads over traditional juniper; unconventional but still gin-like.

critics.nose: Pine buds, spruce, fir and pine cones; immediately evocative.
critics.palate: Sage and bay leaf early, then juniper and fir needle turning minty; coriander, gentle spice and a touch of lemon.
critics.finish: Cool, moderately long, minty sage; very smooth.
critics.summary: Highly recommended; best neat or in a G&T with lime.

facts.mash_bill: Botanicals: Douglas fir, California bay laurel, juniper, wok-roasted coriander, lemon, Seville orange, angelica, orris, sage, Saigon cinnamon, cardamom, fennel seed
facts.cask: Fir and sage distilled separately; bay laurel and juniper vapor-infused

notes: ABV 45% confirmed by producer and Difford's.

producer.summary: Producer gives no formal tasting notes, only calls it very smooth and suitable neat or mixed. Botanicals: cardamom, coriander, French lavender, anise seed, sarsaparilla, juniper and two orange peels; 18-hour maceration then steam-heated distillation.

critics.nose: Sarsaparilla and orange peel that highlight lavender.
critics.palate: Subtle sweetness with juniper pine in a supporting role.
critics.finish: Bittersweet with cinnamon and minty notes.
critics.summary: Suggested for an Aviation, Pegu Club or Bee's Knees.

critics.nose: Faint juniper with coriander and star anise.
critics.palate: White pepper, orange oil and lavender; very gentle.
critics.finish: Tangy and gently expansive.
critics.summary: Rated 2 stars (Recommended) on the site's own star system; soft gin good neat or for vodka drinkers, easily lost in cocktails.

facts.mash_bill: 100% grain neutral spirit; botanicals cardamom, coriander, French lavender, anise seed, sarsaparilla, juniper, two orange peels
facts.cask: 18-hour botanical maceration, steam-heated still, heart cut

notes: No producer nose/palate/finish; critic notes only. Producer site lists Diageo as current owner/distiller.

notes: Producer site unreachable. Master of Malt description (retailer) calls it rich and sweet with nutty notes, stewed plum and a hint of smoke. Natalie MacLean page showed only community notes, no score. Distiller page had no expert review.
